solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Light snow and wider storms around Ohio

indicators.note: something that storms around rages wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
OH is the postal code for Ohio; its first letter O stands for it here

explanation.surface: A weather report: light snow and storms spreading around the state of Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for the snow, but it is the definition. The letters of SNOW and WIDER, with O for Ohio added, are shuffled to give ROSE WINDOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose window is a circular stained-glass window in a church, and a window is a light in architectural terms.

clue.text: Playing through an amp is very exciting

blocks.note: first meaning: amplified, as a guitar plugged in rather than acoustic
second meaning: thrilling, charged with tension

explanation.surface: A musician declares that playing through an amplifier is a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument played through an amplifier is the plugged-in kind, and a thrilling atmosphere is likewise described with this same adjective.

clue.text: When many have lunch outside clubs together

indicators.note: one piece sits outside the other, wrapping round it

blocks.note: at one o'clock, a usual lunchtime
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A note that the lunch crowd heads out to the clubs as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: AT ONE wraps round C, splitting as AT ON-C-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things all at the same moment means doing them simultaneously, which is one sense of together.

clue.text: Dog or rat bites perhaps reported at front

indicators.note: the front of each word means only its opening letter is kept
a mouth that bites closes round what it takes in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a rat is an informer, someone who sings to the police
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A story asking whether it was a dog or a rat whose bites were reported first.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is slang for informing, so a rat is a SINGER. A springer is a breed of spaniel.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer spaniel is a gundog breed, usually just called a springer.

clue.text: Promise of power book ultimately overlooked

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is overlooked, meaning the last one is dropped

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for power
an account book

explanation.surface: A promise of power that, in the end, the book overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn undertaking, a synonym for a promise as a noun.

clue.text: King born in the joint?

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
née, used before a woman's maiden name, means born

explanation.surface: A king born in prison, the joint being slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint of the leg, so it is an example of a joint.

clue.text: Colonel with bit of irksome trapped wind

indicators.note: only a small bit is wanted, the opening letter of the word
something trapped is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An irritated colonel suffering from some trapped wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as flatulence, but it is the verb rhyming with find.
explanation.definitionFit: To coil a rope is to wind it round in loops, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Lady's partner has row about old bouncer

blocks.note: in Disney's Lady and the Tramp, the Tramp is Lady's companion
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A lady's partner gets into an argument about some old nightclub doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel and 'bouncer' a doorman; here the row is a queue and the bouncer is something you jump on. 'About' simply places the row beside old.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a sprung mat that bounces people upward, so it is playfully a bouncer.

clue.text: Can its mockery put off musical group?

indicators.note: being put off means thrown into disorder, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the thirteen letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Asking whether a band's mockery could discourage people.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic Monkeys are an indie rock band from Sheffield, England, so they are an example of a musical group.

clue.text: Criminal after US agency is religious type

indicators.note: one piece coming after another tells the solver which order to write them in

blocks.note: the Drug Enforcement Administration
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: A criminal pursued by US drug agents turns out to be devout.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained church minister ranking below a priest, so a religious figure.

clue.text: Issue scolded soldiers brought about large knight

indicators.note: the words are brought round about another piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: chid is an old past tense of chide
L is the abbreviation for large
the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A tale of scolded soldiers dealing with a big knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Chid is the archaic past tense of chide. 'Issue' looks like a problem, but in law it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's issue means their offspring in legal language, so children is the plural equivalent.

clue.text: PM head of Decca sent to Foreigner

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the opening letter of the record label's name
a foreigner from Israel, as one example

explanation.surface: A record company boss signing the rock band Foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: Decca is a record label and Foreigner a rock band, but here Foreigner stands for one particular nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was twice British Prime Minister in the nineteenth century, so he is an example of a PM.

clue.text: Excessively desirous of good grass? Yes!

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
Y is a shorthand for yes

explanation.surface: Someone longing for quality cannabis, answering yes eagerly.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy describes wanting far more than one needs, so it matches excessive desire.

clue.text: Contrary git puts up with small vagrants' digs

indicators.note: contrary means running the opposite way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a sod is British slang for an unpleasant person, like a git
S is the abbreviation for small
to put someone up is to house them

explanation.surface: An awkward idiot gives shelter, along with a youngster, to vagrants.
explanation.walkthrough: Git and sod are both mild British insults for a contemptible person. DOS and S come first, then HOUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosshouse is a cheap lodging for homeless people, so the plural means rough accommodation for vagrants.

clue.text: Cook flappers picked up in Boots?

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to doctor is to cook, as in falsifying accounts
martins are swallow-like birds, flappers of wings

explanation.surface: A cook who has stuffed flappers into boots.
explanation.walkthrough: Martens are weasel-like animals; martins are birds. The question mark marks Boots as an example, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc Martens are a famous make of chunky lace-up boots, so the brand is an instance of boots.

clue.text: How 11 might be described individually?

blocks.note: first meaning: the numeral 11 is a one written beside a one
second meaning: separately, each in turn

explanation.walkthrough: 11 looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is just the number eleven, two ones side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means taking each person or thing separately in turn, which is a synonym for individually.

clue.text: Discharge leader of Ethiopian ministry

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a ministry is religious work, as in a mission

explanation.surface: A notice that the head of an Ethiopian government department has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a verb about dismissal, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is something released or given off, so it is a synonym for a discharge as a noun.

clue.text: Steer clear of wife involved in suit

indicators.note: being involved in something places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to serve is to suit, as in 'that will serve'
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid a wife who is part of a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests a lawsuit, but it is the verb meaning to fit a need.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to veer sharply aside to avoid something, as one steers clear of an obstacle.

clue.text: Was very angry about government in tatters

indicators.note: about means going round the outside of another piece

blocks.note: to rage is to be furious
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: Someone furious that the government is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged clothes are torn and frayed, which is what being in tatters means.

clue.text: Reactionary lot understood justice in hearing

indicators.note: in someone's hearing, words are taken by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: knew means understood
right is what is just

explanation.surface: Reactionaries who understood that justice was served at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests a courtroom, which fits justice, but it signals the sound of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Right was a resurgent conservative movement of the 1970s and 80s, so its members form a reactionary group.

clue.text: Most extensive documents in Europe and US?

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: Europe and America together make up the West
ID is identity documents

explanation.surface: A question about which documents are most widely used across Europe and America.
explanation.definitionFit: Widest is the superlative of wide, so it means covering the greatest extent.

clue.text: Grotesque individual or a leggy criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A description of an ugly person, or a lanky lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the carved spout on a church, a gargoyle is an ugly person, a grotesque.

clue.text: Age is a number, vacuous Eskimo admitted

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the middle of the word is removed and only its outsides kept
what is admitted is let inside, so it goes within the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the algebraic symbol for a number
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: The saying that age is just a number, with an Eskimo let in.
explanation.walkthrough: A and N enclose EO, giving A-EO-N.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immensely long period of time, so it is a synonym for an age.

clue.text: Mostly speak with others about a flying saucer

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: to talk something over with others

explanation.surface: People mainly talking with each other about a UFO sighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying saucer' suggests a UFO, but it is the athletic disc thrown in field events.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is a heavy disc hurled by athletes, which looks much like a saucer as it flies.

clue.text: Some artists perhaps mind stores after work

indicators.note: letters that have been worked on are reshaped, so they appear in a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Some artists keep an eye on the shops once they have finished their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Modernists were artists of the early twentieth-century avant-garde, so they are one kind of artist.

clue.text: Is indebted to content of audiobook!

indicators.note: an audiobook is listened to, so its content is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the word audiobook contains three letter O's, and the plural of the letter O spoken aloud is 'ohs'

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledging their debt to what an audiobook contains.
explanation.walkthrough: Audiobook holds several O's; heard rather than read, O's sounds exactly like the verb meaning to be in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe is to be in debt to someone, so the third-person form matches is indebted to.
